context: GUARDRAILS: every sub-feature ships only after its gate work-unit records evidence; launchd plist must not embed secrets (it re-reads env-file at run time); no TLS/proxy layer before a real consumer exists. Anti-pattern: treating deferred items as implicitly approved - each needs its gate evidence first.
description: exe.dev-parity polish, each sub-feature behind its own internal gate. (1) launchd LaunchAgent template com.agent-container.<project>.plist re-running agent-run.sh --persistent at login - Apple container has no restart policies, so this is the only reboot-survival path. (2) Named-volume repo mode (--volume-mode named + container cp import) is HARD-GATED on first verifying the reported Apple-container limitation that named volumes cannot be mounted by multiple running containers concurrently, AND on reworking lib/gradle.sh - warmup bind-mounts $PROJECT_DIR (upstream run.sh:408) which does not exist in volume mode; if the concurrency limit is real and painful, record the finding and keep bind mounts. (3) Remote access (Tailscale serve / Cloudflare tunnel to the SSH ports) stays deferred until a second machine actually needs in. (4) Per-agent image split happens only on concrete fat-image size or dependency-conflict evidence - record the evidence in the item before building.

deferrals.reason: w2 gate returned BLOCKED on container CLI 1.1.0 - concurrent mount impossible, so the mode cannot be built as designed
deferrals.resolved_reason: Blocked by empirical platform limitation, not by remaining effort: Apple container 1.1.0's local volume driver backs each named volume with a single raw ext4 block device, so a second concurrent mount hard-fails at VM bootstrap (VZErrorDomain Code=2). Recorded as 'Volume gate verdict: BLOCKED' at docs/spikes.md:918. Bind-mount mode remains the default and is unaffected. Re-open only if a future container release adds a shareable volume driver.
